title: chinas june fuel oil exports bunkers up 55 may data shows 2026 07 20
text:
SINGAPORE, July 20 (Reuters) - China's exports of fuel oil, mainly for marine fuel bunkering, climbed 55% month-on-month in June, customs data showed on Monday, ​reaching the highest in 2026 so far.
Export volumes totalled 2.73 million ‌metric tons in June, or about 577,000 barrels per day (bpd), up 18% from the same month last year, General Administration of Customs data showed.
The boost in volumes during ​June brought the first-half 2026 volumes 7.7% higher year-on-year to 10.87 ​million tons.
Softer prices of low-sulphur marine fuel at key Chinese ⁠ports have drawn more demand for refuelling ships, especially in the second ​half of June, market sources said.
Prices of delivered 0.5% low-sulphur marine fuel were ​about $50 a metric ton cheaper at Zhoushan and Shanghai ports versus prices at regional Asia bunker hub Singapore, based on data from market sources.
Meanwhile, China's imports of fuel oil ​in June recovered after slumping to a record low in May, customs ​data showed.
Imports of fuel oil totalled 982,783 tons in June, up 76% from the previous ‌month, ⁠though still 30% lower than June last year.
Demand for fuel oil from refineries for use as a feedstock remained lukewarm as they opted for cheaper crude.
Imports in the first half of 2026 totalled 9.39 million tons, down 3.6% from ​the same period ​in 2025.
